pages.title: Sixteen Paces
pages.text: Behind the door: a floor of $(thing)void stone$() and four walls, sixteen blocks a side. Nothing breaks them. I spent a day finding that out.$(br2)To leave, I walk into any wall. It tears where I come close, and lets me out by my gate.

pages.title: Nothing Here
pages.text: A shelter at last, and nobody to take it from me. Also no water. No soil I did not carry in. No rain, no night, no morning.$(br2)I asked for a world without them. I was given a world without $(thing)anything$(). Hence the $(l:supply/conduits)supply lines$().

pages.title: Rules
pages.text: On the gate, a room's owner decides what may happen inside: monsters appearing, animals appearing, explosions breaking things.$(br2)All of it starts forbidden. I left it that way for a long time.

pages.title: It Keeps Going
pages.text: The room does not stop when I leave it. Furnaces burn and crops grow whether I watch or not.$(br2)I find that a comfort: something of mine that carries on without being asked to.
